messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service 'gold-team-latency' (INC-20260315-7591). Severity: P1. Triggers: 5xx spike + latency > 3s. Pager: auto-page (rotation: gold-team-rotation). Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-20260315-7591

Alex Chen: acked. I'm looking into logs now.

Alex Chen: hmm looks like the page went to the Gold team but the metric source is search-proxy in prod-us-east-1 — that should go to infra-oncall, not gold-team. Did we change routing rules last night? :thinking_face:

Maria Patel: yes, we deployed the new rotation mapping at 2026-03-15T02:10Z. There was a rename of the schedule from `infra-oncall` -> `gold-team` in the deploy config by mistake (config-as-code).

Sam Rao: confirmed. I can reassign the incident to infra-oncall via PD api. Quick mitigation: re-route pages + add a temporary schedule override to avoid further mispages.

Sam Rao: (commands)
```
# reassign incident to infra-oncall
pd incidents update INC-20260315-7591 --assign "infra-oncall"
# add temporary override for gold-team rotation for 1 hour
pd schedules override add --schedule gold-team-rotation --start now --duration 60 --reason "override while we fix mapping"
```

pagerduty-bot: Incident updated: assigned to infra-oncall. Override created on schedule gold-team-rotation (expires in 1 hour).

Priya (oncall): I'm infra-oncall, taking ownership. Joining Zoom in 2m. Can someone post a one-liner customer impact?

Alex Chen: impact: search-proxy 95th latency spiked from ~120ms -> 4.2s for ~15 minutes starting 02:05Z. Scope: ~8% of traffic in us-east-1; two paying tenants reported elevated error rates (internal alert). No full outage but severe degradation.

Jordan: adding monitoring context: logs show an upstream timeout (nginx) to model-service A at 02:03Z, connection resets increasing. Could be a rolling deploy causing connection pools to drain.

Maria Patel: rollback candidate: revert mapping change (config commit c3f9b2a) that renamed schedule. That should stop future misroutes. I'll open a revert PR and request immediate merge.

Sam Rao: temporary routing change applied. I'm also adding an escalation rule: any further P1s for search-proxy will bypass rotation and page infra-oncall directly.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation policy updated for service search-proxy: bypass rotation enabled.

Priya (oncall): on Zoom, seeing high request latencies and some 502s. Running `service restart model-service` is risky — prefer draining and restarting a small subset first. Alex, can you correlate deploys and pod restarts between 02:00–02:10Z?

Alex Chen: checking k8s events... yes there was a rollout for model-service with image tag `v2.14.1` starting 02:01Z; 30% of pods restarted until 02:06Z. Rolling updates + low connection pool size = timeouts.

Priya (oncall): ok do a canary restart of one replica with increased connection pool and watch metrics. Sam, can you throttle traffic to model-service for a minute?

Sam Rao: throttling a subset via istio route weights now: shifting 20% traffic to the fallback model-legacy for 10m. Command: `kubectl apply -f istio-weight-fallback.yaml`

Jordan: logs improving after weight change. 95th latency back to ~200ms in the canary group. No more 502s for those requests.

Priya (oncall): good. Keeping incident P1 while we stabilize. Action items: 1) Revert schedule rename commit c3f9b2a (Maria), 2) Add PD rule test and CI check to prevent schedule rename without owner (Alex), 3) Update runbook for rotation mapping (Jordan).

Maria Patel: PR opened and merged (revert of c3f9b2a). Configuration now maps search-proxy -> infra-oncall schedule correctly.

pagerduty-bot: Note: schedule mapping reverted; future pages should route to infra-oncall. Existing overrides will expire in 55 minutes.

Alex Chen: validating: sent a synthetic alert to search-proxy (test alert) — routing went to infra-oncall as expected.

Priya (oncall): monitoring looks stable for 12 minutes. 95th latency holding ~220ms, error rate normalizing. Shifting to incident cleanup but keeping note for postmortem.

Sam Rao: thumbs up. I'll remove the temporary override in 30m if stable.

Jordan: adding post-incident tickets: PD-1234 add CI gate for schedule renames; PD-1235 add an automated smoke test that verifies rotation mapping after config deploy.

Priya (oncall): summary for Slack/ops channel: 
- Impact: search-proxy latency spike -> degraded UX for ~8% traffic (us-east-1), two tenants saw errors
- Root cause: config-as-code deploy renamed schedule mapping, causing pages to route to wrong team while underlying infra experienced a rolling deploy-induced spike
- Mitigation: reassigned incident to infra-oncall, created temporary schedule override, shifted 20% traffic to fallback model, reverted config, canary restart for model-service, monitoring stable
- Next steps: CI checks, runbook update, PD rule test, postmortem-session scheduled

Alex Chen: adding a short timeline to the incident ticket and will draft the postmortem.

Maria Patel: small note — let's also add a test that runs after deploy that triggers a synthetic page to validate routing, not just smoke metrics.

Priya (oncall): agreed. Closing the active page in ~40m if no recurrence. Thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-20260315-7591 status: monitoring (assigned: infra-oncall). Next update expected by 02:55Z.

Alex Chen: marking this thread resolved for paging misroute. Will include config diff in postmortem.

Jordan: :eyes: will follow up on runbook edits.

Sam Rao: :white_check_mark: scheduled removal of override at +30m unless flagged.

Priya (oncall): signing off monitoring watch. If anything changes, reopen thread. Good job team.
notes: post-incident: follow-ups filed PD-1234 PD-1235; runbook update assigned to Jordan; CI gate assigned to Alex; config revert commit c3f9b2a-revert
